title: Drying Allowance for Grain Committed to the Cooperative
content:
Grain the member has committed to the cooperative is dried at an allowance, because the cooperative takes the grain in the end, the bushels applied being counted as the net bushels the delivery entry credits to the contract rather than the gross weigh across the scale. The allowance applies to conditioning charges on Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements and is decided from the member's position under Grain Marketing Contracts.

## What the schedule provides

Where ten thousand bushels or more have been applied to the member's marketing contracts in the last three months and the member holds an active marketing contract for the same commodity with bushels still open, the full drying allowance of 10.0 percent is taken off the charge.

Where bushels have been applied to the member's marketing contracts in the last three months, or the member holds an active marketing contract for the same commodity with bushels still open, the modest drying allowance of 4.0 percent is taken off.

And otherwise no allowance is given.

## The two records the allowance is read from

The first is the bushels applied to the member's contracts under Grain Marketing Contracts over the last three months, taken from the delivery entries in that product's ledger that were applied to a contract; the quantity counted on each such entry is the net bushels it credits to the contract, not the gross weigh across the scale. The second is whether an active marketing contract for the same commodity still carries open bushels.

| Bushels applied in the last three months | An active contract for the same commodity with bushels still open | Allowance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10000 or more | yes | 10.0 percent |
| 10000 or more | no | 4.0 percent |
| more than nil but under 10000 | yes or no | 4.0 percent |
| nil | yes | 4.0 percent |
| nil | no | none |

## Worked allowances, on hypothetical figures

**A charge for the pass of 1286.86, with 14000 bushels applied over the three months and an open contract for the same commodity.** The full allowance of 10.0 percent is taken off: 128.686, which rounded to the nearest cent is 128.69.

**The same charge, with 14000 bushels applied but no contract still open.** The modest allowance of 4.0 percent is taken off: 51.4744, which rounded to the nearest cent is 51.47.

**The same charge, with nothing applied over the three months and no contract still open.** No allowance is given.

## Boundary reading

Ten thousand bushels exactly, with an open contract for the same commodity, reaches the full allowance, the threshold being ten thousand bushels or more. A single bushel applied over the three months is enough to reach the modest allowance on its own.
